Rife

RYFE -- one syllable, rhymes with 'knife'. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Rife is widespread and unchecked.

By late summer the harbor town was rife with rumors that the old lighthouse would be torn down.

Worked Example

In the abandoned orchard, weeds choke every row, beetles swarm the trunks, and rot creeps from apple to apple with no one to stop it.

The orchard is rife with pests and decay -- undesirable things spreading everywhere, completely unchecked. Rife describes what is widespread and running free, and it almost always points at something bad.

How Rife Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

rampant

rampant: spreading unchecked and out of control

prevalent

prevalent: commonly found in a place or time

unchecked

unchecked: allowed to continue without restraint

Antonyms

rare

rare: seldom found

absent

absent: not present at all

How Strong Is It? — prevalent → rife → rampant

prevalent vs. rife

prevalent vs. rife: Prevalent is calmer than rife -- a prevalent habit is simply common, while a problem that is rife has spread everywhere and nobody is stopping it.

rampant vs. rife

rampant vs. rife: Rampant is even wilder than rife: corruption that is rife is widespread and unchecked, while rampant corruption is charging ahead, growing more brazen by the day.

Build the Word

The pieces

Put it together

Put it together: Rife survives almost unchanged from Old English rife, 'abundant, widespread,' possibly reinforced by the Old Norse of Viking settlers. It has no common relatives left in modern English -- a lone survivor that has meant 'spreading everywhere' for a thousand years.

Why there's no relative to spot

Why there's no relative to spot: Rife came into English so long ago -- Old English, possibly reinforced by the Old Norse of Viking settlers -- that any word family it once had has died out. There is no cousin word to look for; this is one you learn whole.

Strength Check

Word Choice

Rife rarely sits before a noun; it works after a verb -- 'speculation was rife' -- or in the pattern 'rife with': rife with errors, rife with corruption, rife with mosquitoes. Reserve it for undesirable things: a town can be rife with crime, but never rife with kindness.
